detail.longDescription: I’ve been working on a personal AI image-generation project for the past few days, and I’ve reached a point where I’m struggling to figure out what I’m doing wrong. I’m trying to train a model that can consistently reproduce specific character designs while maintaining their original facial features, proportions, expressions and overall visual style. I’ve collected over 1,600 reference images and have spent quite a bit of time experimenting with the training process, but the results haven’t been what I expected. My biggest issue is facial consistency. The generated images often have completely different face shapes, eye shapes and mouth structures compared to the reference images. I’ve attached a comparison between the original anime images and the AI-generated results to give a better idea of the differences I’m talking about. I’ve experimented with different LoRA weights (1.0, 1.3 and 1.6), but haven’t managed to get satisfactory results. Sometimes increasing the weight actually makes the output worse. I’m starting to wonder if the problem is related to any of the following: Dataset: Image selection, quality, variety or consistency. Image preprocessing: Resizing, cropping and resolution. Captioning: Whether my image descriptions are good enough. Training configuration: Learning rate, epochs, batch size and other settings. Model architecture: Whether I’m using the right approach for this type of training. Generation settings: LoRA weights and inference parameters. I’m hoping to get some advice from people with experience in LoRA training, Stable Diffusion or machine learning, particularly anyone who has worked on character-specific image generation. I’d appreciate any suggestions, insights or recommendations on how to improve the training process and get more consistent results. Any help would be greatly appreciated!
